title: You say you follow Jesus…
paragraphs: …but there’s one command you keep quietly ignoring.
Because this one doesn’t just challenge you.

You can worship loudly.
Serve faithfully.
Post Scriptures.
And still be living in quiet rebellion.
Because the real test was never your volume…
Here’s the verse most people don’t argue with—
“Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.” — Luke 9:23
We love a version of Christianity that saves us…
And so we build a life that looks holy on the outside—
while quietly protecting what God told us to surrender.
That secret you keep justifying in the dark.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
It means say no to the version of you that refuses to bow to Christ.
but resists the authority of the King.
Because this is where most stop.
The word deny in Luke 9:23 carries the idea of disowning.
That means you no longer treat your sinful desires as your identity.
You don’t rename them to make them feel acceptable.
if you’re still in love with yourself.
Our right to choose what we keep and what we give to God.
The life you’re trying to protect… is the very thing keeping you from real life.
This is where shame creeps in.
You know the areas where you’ve resisted God.
You know the compromises you’ve normalized.
You know the voice you’ve been ignoring.

“You’ve gone too far.”
“You’re too divided.”
“You’re not serious enough for God.”
Because this is where everything shifts.
The cross is not just a symbol of suffering.
Jesus didn’t say “deny yourself” so you could destroy your life.
He said it so He could give you a new one.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
“…but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
“But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not when you finally denied everything perfectly.
Jesus lived the life you couldn’t live.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
This is where denial makes sense.
Because Jesus already carried the weight.
You’re not denying yourself to earn love.
You’re denying yourself because you’ve been loved at the highest cost.
Following Jesus is not behavior modification.
“I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me…” — Galatians 2:20
Not to improve your old life.
Your right to define truth on your own terms.
peace that doesn’t depend on your performance.
So let me ask you again.
What are you refusing to deny?
That part of your life you’ve labeled “off-limits” to God.
That’s the battleground of your soul.
And Jesus is not asking for partial access.
He’s asking for all of you.
You don’t carry the cross alone.
“Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28
The power to walk it out.
Stop pretending it’s not that serious.
You might be the interruption they need.
And if something in you is stirring—
that discomfort, that conviction, that pull—
Follow if you’re ready to grow.
